prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

NEW YORK (CNN) -- Two customers are suing Wal-Mart for negligence after being injured in a mad rush for post-Thanksgiving bargains that left one store employee dead, the men's attorney said Tuesday. A temporary worker at this Wal-Mart was crushed to death when shoppers rushed into the store last week. Temporary Wal-Mart worker Jdimytai Damour, 34, was crushed to death as he and other employees attempted to unlock the doors of a store on Long Island at 5 a.m. Friday. Attorney Kenneth Mollins said Fritz Mesadieu and Jonathan Mesadieu were "literally carried from their position outside the store" and are now "suffering from pain in their neck and their back from being caught in that surge of people" that rushed into the Wal-Mart. New York Newsday reported that the Mesadieus are father and son, ages 51 and 19. The lawsuit alleges that the Mesadieus' injuries were a result of "carelessness, recklessness, negligence." In a claim against the Nassau County police department, the men also contend that they "sustained monetary losses as a result of health care and legal expenses ... in the sum of $2 million." "This is a tragic situation that could have and should have been avoided with the exercise of reasonable care. There are very simple measures that could have been put in place to avoid this, such as barriers along the line to spread people out, extra security and a better police presence," Mollins said. He said his clients and others who were at the scene contend that the police "were there ... saw what was happening, and they left." Calls seeking comment from Wal-Mart Stores Inc. were not immediately returned. Lt. Kevin Smith of the Nassau County Police Department said, "it's our policy that we don't comment on open litigations" and would not respond directly to Mollins and his clients' claim that officers left the scene. He said it is "incumbent upon the store to provide security" but noted that there was no security force present when officers responded to an initial phone call after 3 a.m. Friday for an unknown disturbance at the site. Smith said the officers noticed a lack of order with the crowd and began to organize them into a line, remaining on site for about 30 minutes until the crowd had become orderly. Throughout the morning, officers went back to check on the crowd and continued to notice no disturbance, Smith said. He said that there were no additional calls for assistance until about 5 a.m., when people began rushing the doors of the store and trampled Damour. An autopsy showed that Damour died of asphyxiation after being trampled, Nassau County officials have said. Video showed that as many as a dozen people were knocked to the floor in the stampede of people trying to get into the store. The employee was "stepped on by hundreds of people" as other workers attempted to fight their way through the crowd, said Nassau County Police Detective Lt. Michael Fleming. CNN's Kristen Hamill contributed to this report .

**VALLEY STREAM, N.Y.** — Shoppers and family members are pursuing legal action against Wal-Mart following a Black Friday stampede that left a temporary employee dead after being trampled by a crowd rushing to enter the store.

Jdimytai Damour, 34, was working as a maintenance worker at the Valley Stream Wal-Mart on Long Island when a crowd of roughly 2,000 shoppers broke through the store's doors early Friday morning, knocking Damour to the ground and trampling him as they surged inside seeking holiday bargains.

Damour was pronounced dead at a local hospital. Several other people, including a pregnant woman, were injured in the crush.

Witnesses described a chaotic scene as the doors gave way under the weight of the crowd.

"They were like a stampede. Like a bull ranch. It was crazy," one shopper told reporters at the scene.

Attorneys representing Damour's family have filed a wrongful death lawsuit against Wal-Mart, alleging the retail giant failed to provide adequate security and crowd control measures despite knowing large crowds were expected for the pre-dawn shopping event.

"Wal-Mart's inadequate security and safety measures were a blatant disregard for the safety of the public," attorney Kenneth Mollins said in a statement announcing the lawsuit.

Nassau County police are also investigating the incident as a potential criminal matter, though officials have said identifying individual responsible parties within a surging crowd presents significant challenges.

In addition to the wrongful death suit, several shoppers who say they were injured during the crush have indicated they plan to file separate personal injury claims against the retailer.

Wal-Mart issued a statement expressing condolences to Damour's family, calling the incident a "tragic situation" and saying the company was working with authorities on the investigation. The company said it was reviewing its crowd management procedures at stores nationwide.

The incident has reignited debate over Black Friday shopping practices, with critics questioning whether retailers do enough to ensure safety when advertising deep discounts that draw massive early-morning crowds.

Occupational Safety and Health Administration officials confirmed they are also looking into the incident to determine whether Wal-Mart violated workplace safety standards.

This is a developing story. CNN will provide updates as they become available.

Damour, 34, was working as a maintenance employee at the Wal-Mart store in Valley Stream, New York, when he was killed on November 28, 2008. As doors opened for the annual Black Friday sales event, a crowd of roughly 2,000 shoppers surged forward, breaking down the store's glass doors and trampling Damour, who had been attempting to help manage the entrance.

**Against Wal-Mart:**
- The company failed to provide adequate security measures despite historical knowledge of chaotic crowd behavior during Black Friday sales events
- Store management did not implement sufficient crowd-control barriers or staffing to manage the anticipated surge of shoppers

The case drew national attention to the safety practices surrounding Black Friday shopping events, which have become associated with incidents of crowd-related injuries at retail locations across the country. Legal experts noted the case raised significant questions about the legal duty of care owed by retailers to both employees and customers during high-risk commercial events, as well as the responsibilities of law enforcement present at such gatherings.
